document.title: UFS 1-300-02
document.fullTitle: Unified Facilities Supplement (UFS) - Unified Facilities Guide Specifications (UFGS) Format Standard
document.reissuesAndCancels: UFC 1-300-02, Unified Facilities Guide Specifications (UFGS) Format Standard, dated 1 April 2014 with Changes 1-3

subsections.title: Construction Specifications Institute (CSI)
subsections.content: CSI prescribes the use of three parts in each section and a consistent subject matter sequence within each part.

rules.text: CSI recommendations must be followed to the extent practical in UFGS.
When a part has no content, insert "Not used." in the body of the text.

subsections.title: Attachments
subsections.content: Attachments are files included at the end of an individual section Portable Document Format (PDF).

subsections.title: Appendices
subsections.content: Appendices are files included at the end of the specifications package PDF.

rules.text: Do not attach appendices to individual specification sections.

subsections.title: UFGS Master Content Guidance
subsections.content: Write the UFGS Master in a clear, concise, complete, and correct manner.

rules.text: Write the UFGS Master in a clear, concise, complete, and correct manner.
Reference non-Government standards to the greatest extent possible in lieu of repeating their requirements.
UFGS are broad and non-geographical in technical content.
Provide bracketed or tailored options when requirements may vary.
Accompany bracketed or tailored options with designer notes to provide direction on identifying and selecting the appropriate options.

subsections.title: Editing UFGS for Projects
subsections.content: Use the latest version of UFGS. The UFGS are master guide specifications that provide the minimum level of quality.

rules.text: Use the latest version of UFGS in accordance with UFC 1-200-01.
Do not specify lesser quality requirements than provided in the UFGS.
Do not repeat requirements from the drawings.

subsections.title: Electronic File Format
subsections.content: SpecsIntact files are in Extensible Markup Language (XML) format with a SEC extension.

rules.text: Specifications must be in UFGS format, comply with this UFS, and be prepared in SpecsIntact.

subsections.title: Section Numbering
subsections.content: Each UFGS carries a unique section number and title in accordance with the CSI MasterFormat.

rules.text: Each UFGS carries a unique section number and title in accordance with the CSI MasterFormat, Numbers & Titles (latest version).
If a number listed in MasterFormat is used, then use its exact title as listed.

subsections.title: Subpart Numbering
subsections.content: Number subparts within the UFGS in accordance with the numeric system.

rules.text: Do not exceed the sixth level subpart numbering in a section.

subsections.title: Subpart Titles
subsections.content: Subparts must have titles, with formatting rules for case.

rules.text: Subparts must have titles, with full uppercase for the first subpart level (ARTICLE) and title case for lower-level subparts.

subsections.title: Text Paragraphs within Subparts
subsections.content: Limit untitled text paragraphs within a numbered subpart.

rules.text: Use no more than two untitled text paragraphs within a numbered subpart. If there are more than two text paragraphs, either include them in an ordered list (OLG and OLI tags) or create subparagraphs (SPT, TTL, and TXT tags).

subsections.title: Designer Notes
subsections.content: Notes provide directions and criteria for the designer.

rules.text: Provide notes between the subpart title and text paragraph to indicate when to use the paragraph, how to choose bracketed items, and to indicate what tailoring tags are in the text paragraph.
Provide the note within tailoring tags if the note only applies when the tailoring option is selected.

subsections.title: Units of Measure (Metric or English)
subsections.content: For UFGS masters, provide measurements in both metric and English units.

rules.text: For UFGS masters, provide measurements in both metric and English units, with metric units first.
The format is: text<MET> 50 mm</MET><ENG> 2 inches</ENG> text; with no space between the text before the MET tag, a space before the measurement within the tags, and no space between tags.
Provide conversions in accordance with IEEE/ASTM SI 10 or industry practice or standard.
Do not use parenthesis to show both metric and English units.
For projects, avoid using both metric and English units.

subsections.title: Referenced Publications
subsections.content: All publications referenced in the UFGS section subparts are also listed in the REFERENCES Article.

rules.text: All publications referenced in the UFGS section subparts are also listed in the REFERENCES Article.
The Reference Identifier (RID) tag must be used for each publication referenced within the REFERENCES Article and at every occurrence of the publication referenced in the section subpart text.
Publication references found in designer notes do not require the RID tag.
Do not update references before their effective date.

subsections.title: Standards Organizations
subsections.content: Identify standards-producing organizations cited in the section text with the acronym in the UMRL.

rules.text: For UFGS Masters, identify standards-producing organizations cited in the section text with the acronym in the Unified Master Reference List (UMRL).
The RID must include the organization acronym and publication number as stated in the UMRL.

subsections.title: Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Clauses
subsections.content: Avoid referencing FAR clauses.

rules.text: Avoid referencing FAR clauses, as they are provided in the Contract's procurement requirements.
When referencing a FAR clause cannot be avoided, use the FAR number followed by the title (in title case) in the text.
Do not include the date of the FAR clause.
Do not include the FAR clause in the REFERENCES Article.

subsections.title: Reference Dates and Titles
subsections.content: Use the most current standard referenced in the UFGS.

rules.text: Use the most current standard referenced in the UFGS in accordance with UFC 1-200-01 unless a specific reason exists to cite an earlier version.
The reference's title must consist of the year of publication in parenthesis followed by the title as stated in the UMRL.
Separate the date of a reference's revision (R), change (C), or similar edition from the original date with a semi-colon, and exactly as it appears in the UMRL.
Reference industry standards to the maximum extent possible for products and their installation to reduce the written text in the body of the UFGS.

subsections.title: Quoting Reference Standards
subsections.content: Do not quote or repeat portions of the referenced standard.

rules.text: Do not quote or repeat portions of the referenced standard in the text of the guide specifications unless it is necessary to improve clarity and readability.

subsections.title: Cross References
subsections.content: Avoid cross-referencing UFGS sections and paragraphs.

rules.text: Avoid cross-referencing UFGS sections and paragraphs in other UFGS sections or within the same section.
When a section cross-reference is necessary, reference with the following format: Section <SRF>01 23 40</SRF> MISCELLANEOUS (where MISCELLANEOUS is the full Section Title).
When referencing paragraphs within the same section, reference by paragraph title, not by paragraph number.
Do not reference UFC in UFGS sections, with exception to Designer Notes as guidance to the specification editor and designers, and Design-Build projects and its tailoring.

subsections.title: Tailoring
subsections.content: Tailoring options in the UFGS allow pre-editing of information.

rules.text: For clarity in viewing a UFGS in a format other than SpecsIntact, consider providing tailored items as part of a complete sentence rather than items within a sentence.
Along with tailoring options, provide a designer note to identify the tailoring in the text and the criteria for selecting the tailored option.

subsections.title: Service-Specific Tailoring
subsections.content: Reconcile Agency differences to the greatest extent possible.

rules.text: Master UFGS writers must reconcile Agency differences to the greatest extent possible to avoid the need for Service-specific paragraphs within a specification.
Do not use both tailoring and bracketed paragraphs to resolve a particular DoD Service-specific requirement within a specification.
Use caution when brackets and tailoring options are in the same specification. Ensure bracketed options are correctly placed in or out of tailoring options to include all necessary Services.

subsections.title: Design-Build or Design-Bid-Build Tailoring
subsections.content: Tailoring options for design-build or design-bid-build contracts.

rules.text: Ensure that design-only requirements for design-build projects are captured in tailoring tags.
Tailored items should be shown as complete sentences within TAI tags, not as partial words within a sentence.

subsections.title: Brackets
subsections.content: Use brackets for choices of multiple items and for blank options requiring designer input.

rules.text: Use brackets for choices of multiple items and for blank options requiring designer input.
Do not use both tailoring and bracketed paragraphs to resolve a particular requirement within one specification.
Organize bracketed options in the order of the most used item first.
Provide brackets around five blank underscored characters ([_____]) to indicate the designer is to provide wording.
Unless the bracketed choices are known industry practices, provide a designer note to assist in the editing of the bracketed items or filling in the blank.
Apply spacing to brackets in a consistent manner throughout to ensure proper spacing when unselected brackets are removed.

subsections.title: Submittal Items
subsections.content: Submittal item formatting and classification rules.

rules.text: Only submittal items are allowed in the SUBMITTALS Article; do not include instructions or other explanatory text.
Each submittal item must be within one set of submittal tags, for example, <SUB>Item</SUB>.
Do not list multiple submittal items separated by commas within submittal tags.
Double-space submittal items.

subsections.title: Submittal Naming Convention
subsections.content: Use unique names for submittal items.

rules.text: Use unique names for submittal items to differentiate them from each other.

subsections.title: Submittal Items Tagged in the Section Subpart Text
subsections.content: Each submittal item in the SUBMITTALS Article must appear tagged only once outside the SUBMITTALS Article in the section subpart text.

rules.text: Each submittal item in the SUBMITTALS Article must appear tagged only once outside the SUBMITTALS Article in the section subpart text.
Submittal items must appear, within the tags, exactly as written in the SUBMITTALS Article and in the section subpart text with the exception of the case; submittal items are not case-sensitive.
Provide a detailed description of the submittal item and its requirements in the section subpart text, and not in the SUBMITTALS Article.
Do not repeat information already provided in UFGS 01 33 00.

subsections.title: Government (G) Submittals
subsections.content: When a 'G' follows a submittal item, it indicates Government approval is required.

rules.text: Only use a 'G' in submittal tags for items deemed sufficiently critical, complex, or aesthetically significant to warrant approval by the Government.

subsections.title: Writing Style (General)
subsections.content: General writing style requirements for specifications.

rules.text: Write in a direct, active voice with simple, concise sentences.
Avoid ambiguous, indefinite terms such as "too short" or "relatively simple."
Define what applies instead of using "applicable" or other indefinite wording.
Do not use "as shown on the drawings" as this phrase is frequently overlooked.

subsections.title: Mood, Tense, and Voice
subsections.content: Requirements for grammatical mood, tense, and voice in specifications.

rules.text: Use the imperative mood (such as, Install equipment) except when clarity requires the use of the indicative mood (such as, Equipment must).
Speak only to the Contractor, not the subcontractor, supplier, or manufacturer.
Do not use the specification to instruct the Contracting Officer.

Directing the Contractor through subcontractors, suppliers, or manufacturers can be misinterpreted as indicating responsibility. Stating "the manufacturer must provide" could be incorrectly interpreted.

subsections.title: Abbreviations and Acronyms
subsections.content: Rules for using abbreviations and acronyms.

rules.text: Use of abbreviations and acronyms must follow the practices within the discipline involved.
At the first use, write out the term completely and follow with the abbreviation or acronym in parentheses.
Use abbreviations for units such as psi, cfm, and kW, and be consistent in their use.

subsections.title: Units
subsections.content: Rules for numeric values and units.

rules.text: Spell out numbers zero through nine, except units of time and measurement, and use numerals for numbers 10 and above.
Avoid starting a sentence with a number, but when unavoidable, always spell out the number when it is the first word of a sentence.
Do not repeat a spelled-out number with a numeral in parentheses.

subsections.title: Terminology
subsections.content: Prohibited and restricted terminology in specifications.

rules.text: The use of "shall" is prohibited. "Shall" imposes an obligation to act but may be confused with prediction of future action.
Avoid the use of "must". If use cannot be avoided, use "must" to prescribe mandatory requirements, actions, and procedures. "Must" imposes obligation and indicates a necessity to act.

Do not use the word "should" in the specification text for mandatory requirements as "should" implies a recommendation. "Should" may be in designer notes to indicate desirable procedures that are advisory in nature.
Do not use "Contractor must provide", use "Provide". Project specifications are already directed to the Contractor, who is responsible for performing the work as shown and specified.

Do not use the term "furnish" unless only delivery of material to the site is required. Similarly, do not use the term "install" unless the Government or others will furnish equipment or materials and Contractor will install. Use "provide" to mean "furnish and install".

Do not use "to be" for describing work that will be accomplished by the Contractor. "To be" implies that someone will accomplish the work other than the Contractor, such as the Government or another Contractor.
Do not use "proposed", as it can be interpreted to mean future work by others or work not in this Contract.
Do not use the word "per", use "in accordance with".
Avoid the use of colloquial terms or jargon. For example, do not use "deck" for floor, or "head" for toilet.
Eliminate redundant wording such as "conforming to", "all", and "type". For example, when stating "paint doors", all doors are implied.
Do not use indefinite items such as "etc.", "any", and "and/or".

Do not use vague words and phrases or escape clauses such as "in this specification", "as may be required", "as necessary", "an approved type", "as approved/directed/determined by the Contracting Officer", "first class workmanship", "securely", "thoroughly", "suitable", "properly", "good working order", "neatly", "carefully", and "installed in a neat and workmanlike manner".
Do not use long, compound, or hyphenated words such as "hereinbefore" and "hereinafter."
Use the term "Contracting Officer"; do not use terms such as "Officer in Charge of Construction", "Contracting Officer Representative", or "Government Representative".

subsections.title: Symbols
subsections.content: Symbols that must not be used in specifications.

rules.text: Do not use the symbols: ' (foot), " (inch), # (pound), % (percent), degree symbol, + (plus), - (minus), +/- (plus or minus), bullet/dot (by), x (by), / (per), @ (at), & (and). Replace the symbol with the corresponding wording.
Feet and inch symbols are acceptable only when both are in a dimension (for example, 8'-8") and in tables.
Avoid or minimize the use of parentheses and quotation marks.

subsections.title: Pronouns
subsections.content: Rules for pronoun use in specifications.

rules.text: Use pronouns sparingly, if at all; it is better to repeat the noun.

If pronoun use is unavoidable, do not use pronouns like "he", "his", "this", "they", "their", "who", "it", and "which". Use generic "they" and "their" instead of male or female-specific pronouns if they cannot be avoided.

subsections.title: Capitalization
subsections.content: Capitalization rules for key terms.

rules.text: Capitalize "Contractor", "Contracting Officer", "Government", and "Contract" in specifications.

subsections.title: Brand Name Specifications
subsections.content: Restrictions on using brand names.

rules.text: Do not use brand name or restrictive requirements. Use of brand name items is prohibited unless guidance and formal written approval, in the form of a justification and approval (J&A), is obtained from the Contracting Officer.
Any specification section that contains brand name items must include a notice to that effect on the first page of the section.

subsections.title: Brand Name or Equal Specifications
subsections.content: Restrictions on Brand Name or Equal specifications.

rules.text: Do not use "Brand Name or Equal," unless formal written approval, in the form of a justification and approval (J&A), is obtained from the Contracting Officer in accordance with DFARS 206.302-1(c).
If allowed to specify an item as "Brand Name or Equal", clearly identify in the UFGS the salient characteristics which are considered essential to satisfy the requirement, to determine equality.

subsections.title: Warranty Clauses
subsections.content: Restrictions on warranty clauses.

rules.text: Ordinarily, do not include warranty clauses in the UFGS. A warranty clause is any provision that modifies terms of the 1-year warranty required by the Contract clause of the work performed under the Contract.

subsections.title: Contract Clauses
subsections.content: Prohibition on repeating contract clauses.

rules.text: Do not repeat the Contract clauses in UFGS. If these are randomly modified within the specifications, it may weaken or void the Contract clauses.

subsections.title: Specifying New Items
subsections.content: Guidance on specifying new-to-industry materials.

rules.text: Take care in specifying items that have not gained widespread acceptance and use. If service records of new materials do not exist, consult third-party or independent laboratory tests.
Ensure the item specified is not a brand name.

subsections.title: Tables and Forms
subsections.content: Requirements for tables and forms in UFGS.

rules.text: Ensure that the tables do not exceed 100% of the page width.
Verify that URLs in the UFGS are valid and current before publishing the project specifications.

subsections.title: Clerical Repairs
subsections.content: Non-technical modifications to the specification section.

rules.text: Do not document clerical repairs in the Section Header (Banner), Change List or Revision List.

subsections.title: Change
subsections.content: Technical modifications to a specific aspect of the specification section.

rules.text: A change amends no more than 40 percent of an existing issuance (single update or cumulative total of multiple updates).
The number of changes is limited to the number of years in the designated refresh rate of that document, after which, the UFGS must be revised (as a Revision).

subsections.title: Numeric Format
subsections.content: Subpart numbering rules.

rules.text: Subpart numbering to the sixth level must be completely numeric and each numbered subpart must have a title.
Do not exceed the sixth level of numbering in a section.
Below the subpart level, titles are optional, and ordered list item tags (OLI) should be used with an alternating alpha-numeric designation.

subsections.title: Ordered Lists
subsections.content: Multi-level ordered list rules.

rules.text: Multi-level, alpha-numeric, ordered lists are allowed under the subpart level.
Do not manually enter the lettering/numbering sequence when creating ordered lists.
The hierarchy of ordered lists have an alternating alpha-numeric designation with four levels of indentation beginning with the letter "a." at the first level.
Do not use list progression beyond the 4th level.

subsections.title: UFGS Organizational Guidance
subsections.content: CSI Section Format Outline guidance for UFGS organization.

rules.text: Follow the sequence of information provided in the CSI Section Format Outline even when adjusting the paragraph titles to fit the specified subject matter.
Use only those paragraphs that are applicable to the specified subject, and add any applicable requirements not listed.

requiredPractices.practice: Address only the Contractor
requiredPractices.details: Speak only to the Contractor, not the subcontractor, supplier, or manufacturer.

requiredPractices.practice: Spell out acronyms at first use
requiredPractices.details: At the first use, write out the term completely and follow with the abbreviation or acronym in parentheses.

requiredPractices.practice: Spell out numbers zero through nine
requiredPractices.details: Spell out numbers zero through nine, except units of time and measurement, and use numerals for numbers 10 and above.

requiredPractices.practice: Capitalize key contract terms
requiredPractices.details: Capitalize "Contractor", "Contracting Officer", "Government", and "Contract" in specifications.

requiredPractices.details: For UFGS masters, provide measurements in both metric and English units, with metric units first. Format: text<MET> 50 mm</MET><ENG> 2 inches</ENG> text.

requiredPractices.practice: Use RID tags for all referenced publications
requiredPractices.details: The Reference Identifier (RID) tag must be used for each publication referenced within the REFERENCES Article and at every occurrence of the publication referenced in the section subpart text.

requiredPractices.practice: List all referenced publications in REFERENCES Article
requiredPractices.details: All publications referenced in the UFGS section subparts are also listed in the REFERENCES Article.

requiredPractices.practice: Use SRF tags for section cross-references
requiredPractices.details: When a section cross-reference is necessary, reference with the format: Section <SRF>01 23 40</SRF> MISCELLANEOUS (where MISCELLANEOUS is the full Section Title).

requiredPractices.practice: Reference paragraphs by title not number
requiredPractices.details: When referencing paragraphs within the same section, reference by paragraph title, not by paragraph number.

requiredPractices.practice: Use unique submittal item names
requiredPractices.details: Use unique names for submittal items to differentiate them from each other.

requiredPractices.practice: Tag each submittal item in section text exactly once
requiredPractices.details: Each submittal item in the SUBMITTALS Article must appear tagged only once outside the SUBMITTALS Article in the section subpart text.

requiredPractices.practice: Subparts must have titles
requiredPractices.details: Subparts must have titles, with full uppercase for the first subpart level (ARTICLE) and title case for lower-level subparts.

requiredPractices.practice: Limit untitled text paragraphs to two per subpart
requiredPractices.details: Use no more than two untitled text paragraphs within a numbered subpart.

requiredPractices.practice: Use 'provide' to mean furnish and install
requiredPractices.details: Use "provide" to mean "furnish and install".

requiredPractices.practice: Follow CSI three-part section format
requiredPractices.details: CSI prescribes the use of three parts in each section (GENERAL, PRODUCTS, EXECUTION) and a consistent subject matter sequence within each part.

requiredPractices.practice: Maximum six levels of subpart numbering
requiredPractices.details: Each subpart down to the sixth level is numbered. Do not exceed the sixth level subpart numbering in a section.

requiredPractices.practice: Maximum four levels of ordered lists
requiredPractices.details: The hierarchy of ordered lists have an alternating alpha-numeric designation with four levels of indentation beginning with the letter "a." at the first level. Do not use list progression beyond the 4th level.

requiredPractices.practice: Include brand name notice when applicable
requiredPractices.details: Any specification section that contains brand name items must include a brand name notice on the first page of the section.

requiredPractices.practice: Follow Federal Plain Language Guidelines
requiredPractices.details: For additional guidance, see the Federal Plain Language Guidelines (https://www.plainlanguage.gov/guidelines/).
